newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close at record on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close at record on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks hit record highs Monday, propelled by sustained foreign interest in blue chips and news that the government would go ahead with the sale of Banco de Venezuela this Friday, traders said.

The bolsa's 19-share .IBC index rose one percent to close at a life-time high of 4,618.95 as some ten million shares worth 1.2 billion bolivars ($2.55 million) traded, according to preliminary figures.
Among traded issues, 21 rose, ten fell and five ended flat in a session that once again saw foods producer Mavesa heavily bid.

"During the session's last ten minutes, news that Banco de Venezuela's sale would go ahead saw investors scrambling to take positions," said Activalores broker Gonzalo Alonso who saw the market continuing to rise Tuesday.
Mavesa closed ahead 5.00 bolivars at 122.00 bolivars.
Traders also reported strong interest in textile manufacturer Sudamtex, up 1.25 bolivars to close at 56.00 bolivars, and Venaseta stock which closed up 3.00 bolivars at 44.00 and 45.00 respectively.

Among the session's other major trades, Sivensa class B ADRs, which are backed by newly issued Class B shares, traded at a discount to their issue price settling at 1,375.00 bolivars after opening at 1,532.50 bolivars.
